fact: The DIAL expert comment states that Morocco's 2015 adequacy list, a list of countries personal data may be sent to, did not recognise a single African country; the year is the only date given.

The Council of Europe Consultative Committee states that Moroccan law 09-08 (articles 43 and 44) lays down protection of transfers of personal data to foreign countries, in particular where the country does not provide an adequate level of protection; dated 18 October 2012, the document does not give the law's date.

Article 11 of loi n° 05-20 on cybersecurity (dahir n° 1-20-69 of 25 July 2020, Bulletin officiel n° 6906 of 6 August 2020) requires sensitive data to be hosted exclusively on national territory, with fines of 200,000 to 400,000 DH under article 49 for heads of vital entities or infrastructures hosting it abroad; article 53 makes the law operative only on publication of its implementing texts.
system: Loi n° 05-20 relative à la cybersécurité, article 11

fact: Hespress English, citing a Global Finance report, states that a 2021 law mandates sensitive data be stored locally in Morocco; the date is the article's published date, and the article gives no law name.
system: 2021 law mandating local storage of sensitive data (unnamed)

fact: The African Union Commission's status list dated 2026-02-02 shows Morocco with no date of signature, ratification/accession or deposit for the Malabo Convention (20 of 55 states have ratified).
system: African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection
